dedupe_keys.name: restoration of the oka river upper estuary urdaibai biosphere reserve

description: This Climate-ADAPT case study describes the restoration of the upper estuary of the Oka River in the Urdaibai Biosphere Reserve, Biscay, Basque Country, Spain, where a canal and drained marshes had cut the estuary's natural functions. Since 2010 marshland has been recovered, including permanent flooding of the Barrutibaso area, part of the original intertidal channel has been reopened, some dykes and barriers have been removed, and embankments built to create lagoons that will become intertidal zones. Invasive species such as Baccharis halimifolia were eradicated on about 700 hectares, and a 14 km path network, a pedestrian and cycling bridge and an education app were added. Projections cited include sea level rise of 29 to 49 cm by 2100 and up to 30 percent more extreme rainfall, and the 2014 storms eroded the nearby Laida beach. The project cost about 2.5 million euros, fully funded by the Basque Government's environment department. The page, published in 2018 and updated in 2026, is accessible online as free HTML on the Climate-ADAPT portal with a link to the Basque Government project page. Caveats: some dyke removals await permission and some municipalities and landowners did not take part, so the project is incomplete. It illustrates nature-based coastal and river flood hazard reduction and climate adaptation of an estuary; related records are the Hesketh Out Marsh and Hedwige and Prosper polders case studies.
